blocks.content: The primary challenge for IRDAI lies in balancing rapid insurance market growth and innovation with robust policyholder protection and solvency stability.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI faces the dual challenge of increasing low national insurance penetration while ensuring strict market regulation.
Preventing mis-selling of insurance products and ensuring timely consumer grievance redressal remain critical regulatory hurdles.
Maintaining financial stability through a minimum required Solvency Ratio of 150% is mandatory for all operating insurers.
Adapting regulations to fast-paced technological advancements like InsurTech while safeguarding cybersecurity and data privacy is paramount.

rows: Percentage ratio of total insurance premium to Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
Ratio of total insurance premium to total population (premium per capita)
Economic importance of the insurance sector relative to the national economy
Level of insurance awareness and average spend per individual

items: IRDAI was established as a statutory body following the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee (1993).
Insurance Penetration is measured as the percentage of premium to GDP, whereas Insurance Density is the ratio of premium to total population.
The minimum solvency ratio mandated by IRDAI for insurance firms in India is 150%.
